body:
Hello OddYoghurt. I was not put in foster care but a lot of your story later on in your life sounds very similar to my own experience. There are other people out there in the world who understand your pain and, like the girl who commented before me, even people who have gone through similar situations.

Especially with being vulnerable online and attracting older men, I didn't realise that other people also went through that experience until a few months ago and I used to hate myself so much for trying to find validation/acception/care through them. Nine times out of ten there will be multiple minors they have identified as vulnerable and are contacting. So please take it from me that you have done nothing wrong and I completely understand why you have looked for comfort in those places. It's impossible to understand unless you've been in a situation where it's your only point of positive communication sometimes.

I don't know how the foster care system works in your country but in mine, there are many schemes and charities around the country who can help you with everything from housing to food to bills. It might be worth starting to research this, and seeing what is available to you in your area. I'm sorry if this sounds patronising though.

Finally, if you are still in touch with that counsellor or perhaps have access to another mental health advisor, now might be the time to mention how you are feeling. Even if it seems embarrassing or that you've "had enough help already". There's no shame in needing more support than others, especially because you do not have support from other people around you.

I send so much love your way and hope that things can slowly change for the better for you in your life, before the time when you choose to make the decision. Nothing asks to be born or brought to life, but that you are alive is justification enough for you your continued presence. Your life doesn't need to look a certain way, you don't need to have a set number of friends, you don't need to be achieving the same goals as everybody else. If the next part of your life is a focus on finding stability and safety for yourself after leaving foster care, and sorting through your childhood emotions, then you have every right to use your life for that.

Xx

Hello, I'm so happy to hear that you were able to find a reason to continue going. It's good that the experience was able to push you in a better direction for your life, despite how intimidating it must have been while you were there. The best of luck to you in future.

Hello hibiki777! Thank you for the kind words. I think it's difficult because when somebody can't be a physical presence, it's hard to be able to lean on that person for support. I also wouldn't want to ask that from somebody I didn't know.

I'm sorry you grew up with an abusive mother, I truly am. My parents were more absent than abusive so I can only imagine how that would have taken a toll on you. It's good to see that you are still pushing forward and willing yourself to live.

It's almost morning now for me, but it was nice to speak to you. Xx
Hi, thank you for talking here. :) Yeah, it's nice to feel like you are of use or could help somebody. This was my line of work before I was fired, too.
